findings.title: Generated releases become uninstallable after schema v4
findings.why_it_matters: Every newly generated firmware release advertises support for configuration schema 3 only, while the configurator now requires schema 4. The browser therefore rejects the release manifest before flashing starts, so fresh installs and firmware updates cannot reach the timezone fix. Advertising schema 4 in the generated manifest restores agreement between the release pipeline, browser, and firmware.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the generated configuration compatibility range to minimum 4 and maximum 4, then add a release-generator test that feeds its produced manifest to the web manifest validator (or at minimum asserts both generated bounds equal 4).

residual_risks: A v2/v3 record has no device timezone to recover, so migration deliberately falls back to the spot timezone; upgraded devices whose owner timezone differs from the spot remain wrong until their configuration is applied again.

The browser accepts any timezone known to its Intl runtime, while firmware accepts only names present in its embedded TZDB registry; no cross-runtime acceptance check proves every browser-produced device timezone can be installed.
testing_gaps: No end-to-end contract test validates a manifest produced by firmware/scripts/generate_installer_manifest.py with web/src/installer/firmwareManifest.js after the shared configuration version changes.
No firmware render test exercises different device and spot timezones through the production render_dashboard path, including a DST boundary.
